(#6880)

* Don't treat code 1000 as special

Originally introduced in #2832, the close code 1000 was treated as a way to
make the documented "disconnect" broadcast not reconnect in the browser.

See also https://github.com/phoenixframework/phoenix/issues/3161#issuecomment-438457201

The problem is that code 1000 is not always in our control. A middleware
might close a WebSocket connection with code 1000, leaving the browser
permanently disconnected. So using code 1000 is not a realiable meachnism
for this.

Additionally, we recently changed "disconnect" to send 1001 instead,
circumventing the whole thing: https://github.com/phoenixframework/phoenix/pull/6678

With all that in mind, I propose to remove special casing of 1000 completely.
I see two ways we can go forward:

1. Use a custom code, e.g. in 4000-4999 for "disconnect" and document
   that the socket will not reconnect. LiveView can still handle this
   code specially, but instead of reloading with jitter, we can immediately
   reload, as it is most commonly used when disconnecting a single user.
2. Keep "disconnect" reconnecting, as it does now and introduce a new
   "permanent_disconnect" or however it would be called that is documented
   to not reconnect.
